summary: A seat that restarts always is no longer left stopped for good when its launch failed three times: the parked launch is retried after a doubling wait (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 30 minutes, six retries since its last successful launch), each retry reports the failure before it, and a retry that starts the seat clears the fault. The launcher is the first pty on the launch PATH that accepts name-only --env, so an older pty build earlier on the PATH no longer parks restarts

replay.detail: No claim replay or recovery behavior changes for completed operations. A parked launch of a seat that restarts always now records 'retry' and 'retries-exhausted' reconcile decisions (keys runtime-crash-loop-retry:<token>:<n> and runtime-crash-loop-retries-exhausted:<token>); the crash-loop fault is hidden once a retry's launch has succeeded.

schema.detail: No tables, indexes, triggers, schema-version changes or data rewrites. The new decisions use existing runtime.reconcile-decision fields (key, decision, reason, plus owner_run).

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or digest changes; each retry has its own key, so checkpoints keep every retry decision like any other keyed decision.

compatibility.detail: Two new reconcile decision names ('retry', 'retries-exhausted'); readers that treat any decision other than 'member-fault' as a cleared fault are unchanged. An older daemon sharing the log ignores them and keeps the launch parked.

downtime.detail: No additional startup work or expected interruption. A seat parked before the upgrade is retried on its first pass by a daemon with this change when its last failure is more than a minute old.

manual.detail: No operator actions are required; an exhausted launch is restarted with st agents restart as before.

recovery.detail: No persistent state changes or new swap-back restrictions.
